text: Seabrook Town made an impressive comeback to beat Harbour City 4-2 after trailing 2-0 at halftime. Harbour City took an early lead thanks to Elias Okafor and a beautiful long-range goal from Marek Barros, who shone with 1 goal and 2 assists to earn Player of the Match honors [#905] [#975]. Harbour City played patient short passes, building attacks carefully, but a red card to Joon Whitfield late in the first half hurt their defense [#871]. Seabrook Town fought back strongly in the second half with fast counterattacks, scoring four goals. Their switch to pressing higher and playing more direct overwhelmed Harbour City late, with Kian Romano scoring twice in injury time, including a killer goal after a smart short-pass move [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook Town created more and better chances overall, showing how their wide, crossing style produced 9 corners and more touches in the box. The match was a thrilling display of tactical changes turning the game around!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in en

- Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 over Harbour City despite initially trailing 2-0 at half time [#905, #975, #1104].
- Marek Barros scored and assisted for Harbour City, earning Player of the Match with a rating of 9.8 [#975].
- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals in the second half with notable contributions from Kian Romano who scored twice late in added time [#1448, #1882, #1906].
- Seabrook Town had a higher xG total of 3.44 compared to Harbour City's 1.03, reflecting more high-quality scoring chances [team_stats].
- Harbour City's Joon Whitfield received a red card at 43', reducing their defensive capacity [#871].

- Harbour City played a 4-2-3-1 formation focusing on patient short passing, evidenced by a 17-pass, 56.9-second build-up leading to their first goal by Elias Okafor at 45'[#904,#905]. This possession-based approach allowed them to maintain control and create a big chance despite a relatively low xG per shot.
- Seabrook Town utilized a 3-4-3 formation emphasizing wide, crossing play, reflected in their nine corners and higher number of box touches (60 vs. 41 for Harbour City), supporting an attack style oriented on width and delivery into the box[#team_stats].
- The comeback by Seabrook Town was initiated by fast regains and direct counterattacks, as seen in Tariq Marlowe's goal at 53' which came after a quick regain and almost immediate finish with zero passes in the buildup[#1103,#1104]. This suggests they used pressing traps to force errors and transition quickly.
- Seabrook’s tactical change at 65'—pressing higher, playing more direct, and increasing line height—correlates with their successful late goals[#1361]. This switch likely aimed to overload the opponent defensively and expedite transitions, taking advantage of their 3-4-3 shape's natural width and forward thrust.
- The last two Seabrook goals involved quick counters and short passing combinations, with the late equalizer at 90+2' stemming from a regain and 2-pass buildup leading to a through ball[#1881,#1882]. The follow-up goal after their pressing intensification featured short passes in open play, signaling effective exploitation of space generated by their high press and wide attacking formation[#1905,#1906].
